purpose: Targeted visible-browser audit of high-risk ranked-domain homepages before provider execution
method: Codex in-app Chromium browser, visibly rendered anonymous root-page load; accessibility tree inspected; no clicks or recursive navigation
scope_note: This is a targeted audit, not a replacement for the full independent headless Chromium capture.

checks.finding: Consistent with an entry page. Localized footer text varies by execution region, so the rule should require only the observed product identity.
The anonymous page displayed a public video recommendation feed. Video titles, channels, views and upload times are dynamic and are not frozen.
Anonymous chat composer and product navigation were visible; the page was not login-only.
The anonymous storefront, search control, departments and product merchandising were visible; current promotions and prices remain volatile.
The public portal and news lists were visible without authentication; headlines, weather and rankings remain volatile.
The public NAVER search surface loaded. The targeted snapshot confirmed page identity but did not replace the fuller headless capture.
The public search entry and hot-search module were visible; current hot-search members are not frozen.
The anonymous public post feed and community links were visible; the page was not a login-only or verification page.
The public marketing page, membership form, benefit sections and FAQ were visible; the page was not login-only.
The public multi-section news homepage and article links were visible; current headlines are not frozen.
The visible-browser environment declined this domain under its site-safety policy. No workaround was attempted; the existing independent headless capture remains the only evidence for this case.
